practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string only from an environment variable or secret store at runtime and never commit, log, or embed the literal URI/credentials in code or repository files.
practices.prior_belief: Read the connection string only from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never commit, log, or store the literal URI/credentials in code or repository files.

practices.practice: Always use TLS for connections to an Azure DocumentDB cluster (include tls=true in the connection string) and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Use TLS/SSL for all connections and validate server certificates (enable ssl=true / tls=true and disable insecure certificate validation) in the Mongo/Mongoose connection options.

practices.practice: Authenticate to Azure DocumentDB using SCRAM-SHA-256 (the MongoDB SCRAM mechanism) and avoid using broad admin credentials in application code; prefer least-privilege users or managed identities and store secrets in Key Vault.
practices.prior_belief: Do not use the cluster admin credentials in the application; create a least-privilege database user (or managed identity/Key Vault-stored credentials) and rotate credentials regularly; read secrets from Key Vault or secure environment variables, not from files.

practices.practice: Choose a shard/partition key that localizes all events for a given paymentReference to the same logical partition (e.g., partition key = paymentReference) so timeline aggregation can be single-partition and efficient.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a partition/shard key that keeps all events for a given paymentReference in the same logical partition (e.g., partition key = paymentReference) to make timeline aggregation single-partition and efficient.

practices.practice: Model audit events as immutable documents with a unique event identifier and a creation timestamp (createdAt); include paymentReference and an ordering field (e.g., stageSequence or stageTimestamp) so the timeline can be deterministically ordered.
practices.prior_belief: Model each audit event as an immutable document with a unique eventId (UUID) and createdAt timestamp; include paymentReference and a numeric stageSequence to guarantee deterministic ordering independent of clocks.

practices.practice: Enforce immutability/idempotency by using a unique key for events (for example _id or eventId) and prefer insert-if-not-exists patterns (upsert with $setOnInsert or conditional insert) rather than relying on update-based mutation.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce immutability and idempotency by (a) using a unique index on eventId and (b) performing inserts as upserts with $setOnInsert or insert-if-not-exists patterns rather than update-based mutation.

practices.practice: Make writes idempotent at the application level by including a client-supplied idempotency/eventId (for example as _id) and deduplicating via a unique index or conditional insert so retries do not create duplicate events.
practices.prior_belief: Make writes idempotent at the application level: include a client-supplied idempotency/eventId and deduplicate using a unique index or conditional insert so retries do not create duplicate events.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Node.js

practices.practice: Create a compound index following the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) to support the timeline query, e.g., { paymentReference: 1, stageTimestamp: 1 } (or paymentReference + stageSequence + createdAt) so a match on paymentReference plus sort is covered and avoids blocking in-memory SORT stages.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound index that supports the timeline aggregation: { paymentReference: 1, stageSequence: 1, createdAt: 1 } (or paymentReference + createdAt) so $match on paymentReference and $sort by stageSequence/createdAt can be covered and avoid in-memory sorts.

practices.practice: Ensure index creation is executed on the server (createIndexes / Mongoose ensureIndexes) and verify completion with explain() or listIndexes; if an external tool like MCP fails to create an index, create it via the official driver and wait for the build before relying on it.
practices.prior_belief: Ensure index creation is executed on the server (createIndexes or Mongoose ensureIndexes) and verify completion with explain() or listIndexes; if a tool (MCP) fails, fall back to createIndexes via the official Mongo API/driver and wait for the index to finish building before relying on it.

practices.practice: For timeline aggregation pipelines, push $match and $project as early as possible, ensure the pipeline can use an index (verify with explain('executionStats') to avoid COLLSCAN), and set allowDiskUse:true when the pipeline is likely to exceed memory.
practices.prior_belief: For timeline aggregation pipelines, push $match and $project as early as possible, and ensure queries use the index (explain('executionStats') should show an index plan and not a COLLSCAN); enable allowDiskUse:true if pipelines may exceed memory.

practices.practice: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter for transient network or throttling errors; limit retries and avoid blind retries on writes unless you have idempotency keys.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter for transient network or throttling errors (check error codes for transient vs permanent), and limit retries; do not retry writes blindly without idempotency keys.

practices.practice: Provision appropriate compute/tier/throughput (or use autoscale) to handle expected write bursts and monitor RUs/OPS; set alerts for RU throttling and high latency to act before ingestion is impacted.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput (or choose autoscale) to support expected write bursts from audit events and monitor RU/OPS; set alerts for RU throttling and high latency so you can increase throughput before tail latency impacts ingestion.

practices.practice: Keep audit event documents small and focused (avoid embedding large binary blobs); store large attachments in blob storage and include a reference in the event document to reduce document size and indexing/write costs.
practices.prior_belief: Keep small, focused documents for audit events (avoid embedding large binary blobs) and store any large attachments in blob storage with a reference in the event document to reduce document size and indexing cost.

practices.practice: Use Mongoose schema validation (required fields, enums for stage names, types) and set strict mode to reject unexpected fields to prevent malformed or partial audit events being recorded.
practices.prior_belief: Use Mongoose schema validation (required fields, enums for stage names, types) and set strict mode to reject unexpected fields to prevent malformed or partial audit events being recorded.

practices.practice: Do not rely only on application-layer immutability hooks; restrict DB user privileges and use least-privilege roles so the application account cannot perform update or delete operations if possible.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid relying solely on application-layer hooks to enforce immutability; where possible restrict DB user privileges so the application account cannot perform update/delete operations, or use database-side controls (roles/privileges) to reduce the blast radius if app code has a bug.

practices.practice: When using vector search features, create vector indexes only on the specific vector field(s) needed, choose the index subtype by scale (DiskANN / HNSW / IVF), normalize embeddings for cosine similarity, and tune index parameters (lBuild / lSearch / maxDegree / product quantization) to match vector dimensionality and query patterns.
practices.prior_belief: If using vector indexes/features, only create vector indexes on the specific vector field(s) needed and tune index parameters (metric, M/HNSW params, dimensions) to match your vector size and query patterns; do not enable global vector indexing by default.

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') on representative queries (e.g., timeline aggregation) and check metrics like keysExamined/docsExamined to confirm index usage; if you see COLLSCAN, add or change indexes or adjust partitioning.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain('executionStats') on representative queries (timeline aggregation) and check metrics (index usage, docsExamined) to confirm the index is used; if you see COLLSCAN in production increase index coverage or adjust partitioning.

practices.practice: Enable automatic backups and choose a retention policy appropriate for audit data (Azure DocumentDB automatic backups are retained for days by default — e.g., 35 days on active clusters) so you can recover from accidental deletion or corruption.
practices.prior_belief: Enable backups and a retention policy appropriate for audit data (or continuous backups/point-in-time restore) so you can recover from accidental deletion or corruption of audit records.

practices.practice: Instrument and emit metrics (ingest rate, write latency, failed inserts, index build time) and logs (do not log secrets) and create alerts for unusual drops in event ingestion rates or spikes in failures.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and emit metrics (ingest rate, write latency, failed inserts, index build time) and logs (do not log secrets) and create alerts for unusual drops in event ingestion rates or spikes in failures.

practices.practice: When using Mongoose or drivers, create a singleton MongoClient (module-level) and configure connection pooling/timeouts appropriate to the environment (serverless: small pools, low minIdle; long-running servers: larger maxPoolSize), and set modern driver options to avoid connection storms.
practices.prior_belief: When using Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB/Mongo API, explicitly set modern driver options (useUnifiedTopology: true, useNewUrlParser: true) and configure connection pooling (maxPoolSize) and timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS) to avoid connection storms on cold start.

practices.practice: For scale-out, pick partition keys and design indexes for even distribution (avoid low-cardinality keys) and validate distribution after seeding traffic with metrics; change the key only after understanding re-shard cost.
practices.prior_belief: If you expect large volumes and need scale-out, design your partition key and indexes for even distribution (avoid low-cardinality keys such as a fixed tenant or stage) and validate distribution with metrics after seeding traffic.

practices.practice: Make seed and verification scripts idempotent: create collections and indexes if-not-exists, insert sample events with a deterministic _id or upsert with $setOnInsert so repeated runs do not insert duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: For seed and verification scripts, make them idempotent: create collections and indexes if-not-exists, insert events with unique eventId or upsert with $setOnInsert so repeated runs do not create duplicates.

practices.practice: Use server-side explain() and the cluster's management tools (DocumentDB MCP server or Azure Portal metrics) to validate index builds and query plans; if a management tool fails to create an index, create it via the official Mongo driver and re-run explain to confirm improvement.
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side explain and the cluster's management tools (the documentdb MCP or Azure Portal metrics) to validate index builds and query plans; if a provided MCP tool fails to create an index, use the official Mongo driver and then re-run explain to prove improvement.

practices.practice: Consider TTL indexes only if business/legal policy permits deletion of audit data; otherwise treat audit documents as append-only and provision storage accordingly.
practices.prior_belief: Consider retention via a TTL index only if business/legal policy allows deletion; otherwise treat audit documents as append-only and provision storage accordingly.
